subject: Computer Networks
note: Comes up more than people expect, especially for backend and infra roles. Know the OSI/TCP-IP layers at a high level, the TCP three-way handshake, the difference between TCP and UDP, and what actually happens between typing a URL and a page loading (DNS lookup, TCP/TLS handshake, HTTP request/response).

subject: AWS Fundamentals
note: You don't need every service - know the core four cold: EC2 (compute), S3 (object storage), RDS (managed relational databases), and IAM (permissions). Understanding the difference between a security group and a VPC is a common follow-up.

subject: Java Core Concepts
note: Beyond OOP basics, be ready to explain the JVM memory model (stack vs. heap), how garbage collection actually works at a high level, and the difference between an interface and an abstract class - a question that comes up constantly.

subject: Kubernetes
note: Increasingly expected even outside pure DevOps roles. Know what a Pod, a Deployment, and a Service actually are and how they relate to each other - that's usually enough to hold your own in a general technical screen.
